architecture: D1 (src/app/allIn-trailingBuy-postExitContinuation.ts rules) adapted to the BTC clock
engine: btcusdt-d1-v1: reference src/btcusdt-d1/engine.ts, fast replay src/btcusdt-d1/fast.ts

units.targetPercentChange: percent string, 0.1-point grid: decline of a completed minute close from the L-day reference high that arms a trailing buy
units.trailingBuyPercentage: percent string, 0.1-point grid: rebound of a completed minute close above the trailing low that sends the buy
units.trailingStopPercentage: percent string, 0.1-point grid: trailing stop below the post-entry high, set once per UTC day from completed days
units.maximumHoldDays: whole UTC calendar days: UTC calendar days from the entry day after which the losing-position exits apply
units.tickWindowSize: whole UTC calendar days: completed UTC days in the rolling reference high (the current day never included)
units.intradayLossBuffer: percent string, 0.1-point grid: net loss, as a share of the entry notional, that sells from the hold day
units.pullback: percent string, 0.1-point grid: decline from the post-exit high that arms within the continuation window
units.continuationWindow: whole UTC calendar days: UTC calendar days after a profitable exit during which the pullback can arm

calendar: UTC calendar days (00:00:00 UTC boundaries), 24/7 trading, decisions at completed minutes
venue: BTCUSDT spot minute bars of unverified venue provenance (consistent with Binance spot; no local metadata)
account: cash-funded spot: 100,000 USDT start, at most 100,000 USDT gross notional per entry, no borrowing, no leverage, cash earns 0
costScenario: principal: fee 10 bps + impact 5 bps per side; stops at min(stop, the next traded minute’s open), recorded at that minute (the next day’s first trade if the trigger is the day’s last minute)
